parts.problemMd:
The image below shows a house mouse, whose scientific name is *Mus musculus*.

![1-1-image-1-mouse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/1-characteristics-and-classification-of-living-organisms/1-1-characteristics-classification-and-features-of-organisms/assets/019-1-1-image-1-mouse.png)

Which genus does it belong to?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** (****Mus****) because:**

- In the binomial system of naming developed by Linnaeus, the first name of the two is the genus that the organism belongs to. It is always written with a capital letter
- The second name is the name of its species and always has a small initial letter. Both should be *italic*ised

**A** is incorrect because mammal is the class that the house mouse belongs to.

**B** is incorrect because musculus is the species name (it begins with a lower case m).

**D** is incorrect because a vertebrate is the phylum that the house mouse belongs to.

parts.problemMd: Which of the following would not be a characteristic seen in all living organisms?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** (photosynthesis) because:**

Photosynthesis is a characteristic shown only by green plants and algae; this is how they obtain their food. It is not a characteristic shown by all organisms.

**A** is incorrect because all cellular life on Earth has the ability to reproduce itself in some way.

**B** is incorrect because all cellular life on Earth must be able to respire in some way to release energy to fuel cellular activities.

**C** is incorrect because all cellular life on Earth must be capable of removing waste products to prevent them from building up and becoming toxic or harmful to the organism.

parts.problemMd: Which name can be given to a group of organisms that have similar morphological features and can reproduce successfully to produce fertile offspring?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** (species) because:**

Members of the same species usually look similar or share similar features, and crucially, can reproduce to produce offspring that can in turn go on to produce fertile offspring themselves.

**A** is incorrect because a kingdom is an extremely large group containing different phyla. For example, animals make up one kingdom, plants make up another.

**B** is incorrect because a genus is a group containing several different species with similar characteristics and evolutionary history.

**C** is incorrect because a family is a taxonomic classification between order and genus; a family contains many different genera.

parts.problemMd:
A yeast (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae),* glucose and water are mixed in a test tube.

The diagrams show the test tube at the start and after one hour.

![1-1-image-4-yeast](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/1-characteristics-and-classification-of-living-organisms/1-1-characteristics-classification-and-features-of-organisms/assets/023-1-1-image-4-yeast.png)

Which process causes this change?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** (respiration) because:**

Yeast is a living organism that can respire both aerobically and anaerobically. The gas carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) is always produced as one of the waste products, the main point of the reaction being to release energy. The bubbles of gas seen after one hour are bubbles of carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>).

**A** is incorrect because reproduction is the process by which more of the same kind of organism is made and doesn’t directly result in the release of carbon dioxide.

**C** is incorrect because growth is a permanent increase in size and dry mass caused by an increase in cell number or cell size (or both).

**D** is incorrect because sensitivity is the ability to detect or sense stimuli in the internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses.

parts.problemMd: Which class of vertebrate typically gives birth to live young?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** (mammals) because:**

Mammals are generally the only group of vertebrates to give birth to live young.

**B, C** and **D** are all incorrect because all other vertebrate classes tend to lay eggs.

parts.solutionMd: **Final answer:** **The correct answer is C.**

parts.problemMd: What is a characteristic of all living organisms?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- This is because sensitivity is a characteristic of all living organisms, which refers to the ability to respond to environmental stimuli, like light, heat, sound, or chemical signals. For example, a plant detects a light stimulus and carries out a growth response to the stimulus by growing toward the light source

parts.problemMd:
Scientists discover a new species of animal.

It has a segmented body with two pairs of legs on each segment.

To which group of animals does this new species belong?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D****.**

- This description points specifically to myriapods, a group of arthropods that includes millipedes and centipedes, which have a segmented body with two pairs of legs on each segment.

**A **is incorrect because arachnids, like spiders and scorpions, have a body divided into two main parts and only four pairs of legs total, not on each segment.

**B **is incorrect because crustaceans, such as crabs and lobsters, often have a hard exoskeleton and a variable number of legs, but not two pairs per segment.

**C **is incorrect because insects have a three-part body (head, thorax, abdomen) with only three pairs of legs total, they do not have two pairs of legs per segment, nor are they as segmented as myriapods.

parts.problemMd:
A scientist observes four events in an organism:

1. It takes in glucose.
2. It releases carbon dioxide produced in cells.
3. It moves away from a harmful chemical.
4. It increases in biomass over time.

Which row correctly matches the events to characteristics?

|   | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | respiration | excretion | sensitivity | growth |
| **B** | nutrition | excretion | sensitivity | growth |
| **C** | nutrition | respiration | movement | reproduction |
| **D** | excretion | nutrition | sensitivity | growth |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B****.**

- **1 = nutrition**: taking in glucose is taking in material for energy
- **2 = excretion**: releasing carbon dioxide produced by cells is removing a waste product of metabolism
- **3 = sensitivity**: moving away from a harmful chemical is detecting and responding to a change in the environment
- **4 = growth**: increasing in dry mass over time matches the definition of growth

While it is possible to link statement 2 with respiration, and statement 3 with movement, the combination given by option B is the only one that is correct for all four statements.

parts.problemMd: Which of the following orders would be correct showing the size of structures from biggest to smallest?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** (stomach → red blood cell → nucleus → chromosome →  gene) because:**

- Genes are the smallest structures shown; genes are ‘coding’ sections of DNA
- A chromosome is formed from a relatively long piece of double-stranded DNA; chromosomes are found inside the nucleus of cells and therefore must logically be smaller than a single cell
- Red blood cells do not contain nuclei, but they are bigger than them
- The stomach is an organ and so logically is the biggest structure listed

The other answers are incorrect because they do not show the correct size order of the structures.

parts.problemMd: Which of the following terms would be correct to describe a leaf, a root and stem?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** (organ) because:**

All three structures in the question are organs. An organ is a group of two or more tissues working together to carry out a particular function.

**A** is incorrect because each of the leaves, stems and roots are made up of thousands of different cells all working together.

**B** is incorrect because the **leaf** is made from **palisade** & **spongy** mesophyll tissue, **epidermal** tissue and **vascular** tissue functioning together to allow a plant to photosynthesise. The **roots** and **stem** are made from **vascular** (transport) **tissue** which work together to transport substances around the plant.

**D** is incorrect because together plants have two organ systems. The** shoot organ system **in a plant is made from leaves, stems, buds, fruits and flowers. The **root organ system** of most plants are all the parts that are underground.

parts.problemMd:
An image of a cell is 24 mm long. The actual cell length is 6 μm.

What is the magnification?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D.**

- The cell is magnified 4000 times

To calculate magnification:

- Convert the units so that they match

  - There are 1000 μm in 1 mm

24 x 100 = 24 000 μm

- Use the formula:

**magnification = image size ÷ actual size**

= 24 000 ÷ 6

=** 4000**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always check that your units match before you begin calculating. If the image size is given in millimetres and the actual size is given in micrometres, convert the image size to micrometres first (multiply by 1000) before doing anything else.
> 
> Carrying out unit conversions at the start of your working reduces the risk of forgetting to convert at all, which is one of the most common sources of error in magnification questions.

parts.problemMd:
The micrograph below shows onion root cells undergoing various stages of mitosis. A x200 magnification was used.

![Microscopic view of plant cells showing nuclei, with an arrow indicating a 1.73 cm measurement. Cells are arranged in a grid-like pattern.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/2-organisation-of-the-organism/2-1-cell-structure-and-size-of-specimens/assets/023-microscopic-view-of-plant-cells-showing-nuclei-w.jpg)

Nathalie Russell via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File:Mitosis_in_Onion_Root_various_stages_(Metaphase).jpg&oldid=801253780)

Which of the following shows the the real length of the cell indicated in the image, rounded to the nearest whole number?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C.**

- Convert the image size from cm to mm

  - 1 cm = 10 mm

1.73 x 10 = 17.3

- Convert from mm to µm

  - 1 mm = 1000 µm

17.3 x 1000 = 17 300

- Note the magnification equation:

$\mathrm{magnification}=\frac{\mathrm{image} \mathrm{size}}{\mathrm{actual} \mathrm{size}}$

- Rearrange the equation to give actual size:

$\mathrm{actual} \mathrm{size}=\frac{\mathrm{image} \mathrm{size}}{\mathrm{magnification}}$

- Substitute the values:

Actual size = 17 300 ÷ 200

= 86.5

- Round to the nearest whole number

=** 87** µm

**A** is incorrect as it results from converting mm to micrometres by multiplying by 100 instead of 1000, giving 8.65 μm which rounds to 9 μm.

**B** is incorrect as it results from dividing the image size by the magnification without converting to micrometres. A further clue that this answer is incorrect is that it has not been rounded to the nearest whole number, as the question requires.

**D** is incorrect as 86.5 μm rounded to the nearest whole number is 87, not 86.

Remember osmosis requires a partially permeable membrane separating two solutions (in living organisms this is a cell membrane). Water molecules can move across the membrane easily, whereas solutes like salts and sugars (e.g. sucrose) cannot.

parts.problemMd: How does a water vapour molecule move out of the air space of a leaf into the atmosphere on a dry day?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** (Diffusion) because:**

Water vapour is just water molecules in the gaseous state; in the leaf water vapour forms when water molecules evaporate from the surface of spongy mesophyll. All gas molecules move by diffusion – the movement of molecules and ions from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration down a concentration gradient as a result of random movement.

**A** is incorrect because active transport requires protein molecules embedded within a membrane using energy released via respiration to move molecules deliberately into the cell (usually against a concentration gradient).

**C** is incorrect because evaporation occurs at the surface of spongy mesophyll cells in the leaf, liquid water changes state to water vapour (a gas).

**D** is incorrect because transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves by evaporation of water at the surfaces of the mesophyll cells followed by diffusion of water vapour through the stomata.

parts.problemMd: What causes the diffusion of carbon dioxide out of a living cell?
parts.solutionMd:
**The correct answer is ****B**** (Random movement of molecules) because:**

Molecules like carbon dioxide must be able to move to be able to diffuse. Individual molecules move about randomly, but overall net movement of a gas occurs from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.

**A** is incorrect because active transport requires protein molecules embedded within a membrane using energy released via respiration to move molecules deliberately into the cell (usually against a concentration gradient).

**C** is incorrect because respiration as a chemical process produces the waste gas carbon dioxide, but the reaction isn’t responsible for the movement of the gas.

**D** is incorrect because photosynthesis is a chemical process that requires carbon dioxide, and although a plant cell photosynthesising lowers the concentration of carbon dioxide inside the cell, it doesn’t cause the movement of carbon dioxide out of the cell.

parts.solutionMd:

**B** and **C** are incorrect because the bronchioles and atria are not adapted for diffusion at all due to their thick walls.

parts.solutionMd:

Active transport requires carrier proteins in the cell membrane, moves particles from lower to higher concentration, and is an active process that requires energy from respiration

**A** is incorrect because particles do not move from a higher concentration to a lower concentration during active transport.

**B** is incorrect because active transport does not involve movement from a higher concentration to a lower concentration, and does use energy from respiration.

**D** is incorrect because active transport does not involve movement from a higher concentration to a lower concentration, and does occur through a cell membrane.

parts.problemMd: By which process do oxygen and carbon dioxide move between cells and capillaries?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B.**

- Oxygen and carbon dioxide move between cells and capillaries by diffusion, which is the process by which particles move from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
- In this case, oxygen diffuses from the blood in the capillaries (where its concentration is high) into cells (where its concentration is lower), while carbon dioxide moves in the opposite direction, from cells to capillaries.

**A **is incorrect because breathing is the physical process of inhaling and exhaling air, moving oxygen into the lungs and carbon dioxide out.

**C **is incorrect because excretion is the removal of waste products from the body (e.g., urea via the kidneys). While carbon dioxide is a waste product, the process of moving gases between cells and capillaries is not excretion.

**D **is incorrect because respiration is the process by which cells produce energy from glucose and oxygen, releasing carbon dioxide as a byproduct.

parts.problemMd:
A chemical test is carried out on a flax seed as follows:

3. The mixture is allowed to settle for about 3 minutes and poured into a second test tube containing water
4. A milky/cloudy layer forms at the top of the test tube

Which of the following correctly names the test and the molecule that it tests for.
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D.**

- The emulsion test is used to detect lipids in a sample
- As the test tube contains a milky/cloudy emulsion, the flaxseeds must contain lipids which are soluble in ethanol

**A** is incorrect because a positive result of the Biuret test for proteins is a colour change from blue to lilac, not formation of a cloudy emulsion.

**B** is incorrect because a positive result of the iodine test for starch is a colour change from brown to blue-black, not formation of a cloudy emulsion.

**C** is incorrect because, while the test described does involve ethanol, it is called the emulsion test (not the ethanol test) and it detects lipids broadly, not oils specifically.

A strand of DNA is shown below:

**T ― G ― A ― A ― C ― T ― A ― G ― C ― C**

What would the correct order of bases be on the complementary strand of DNA?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D ****because:**

DNA consists of a double strand of nucleotides. The bases in the nucleotides can be adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C) or guanine (G). The size of the bases ensures that A always pairs with T and C always pairs with G.

**A **is incorrect because the fifth base, C in the given strand, is paired with A  in the corresponding strand.

**B **is incorrect because this option shows T paired with C and A with G, which is incorrect.

**C **is incorrect because the corresponding strand has the same bases as the given strand.

The DNA strand would look like this:

**T ― G ― A ― A ― C ― T ― A ― G ― C ― C**

**A ― C ― T ― T―  G ― A ― T ― C ― G ― G**

parts.problemMd:
In a length of DNA, 20% of the bases were T.

What is the percentage of base G in this length of DNA?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C****.**

- If C & G make up 60% then dividing this by 2 means that just G makes up 30% of the bases in the DNA

parts.problemMd:

![5-q3-temperature](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/5-enzymes/5-1-enzymes/assets/034-5-q3-temperature.png)
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B ****because:**

- For most enzymes found in living organisms, the optimum (highest rate of enzyme activity) temperature is usually between 30°C to 50°C
- **Increasing** the **temperature** from 0°C  to 50°C would increase the **activity** of the enzyme as the more **energy** the molecules have the **faster** they move, and the number of successful **collisions** between substrate molecules and enzymes increases, leading to the reaction taking less time to occur (increasing the rate)
- Heating to high temperatures (**beyond** the **optimum**) will **break/**alter the bonds that hold the enzyme together and it will lose its shape. This is known as **denaturation**. Substrates cannot fit into the active site of denatured enzymes as they have lost their complementary structures, so above optimum temperatures there is a **rapid** **decrease** in enzyme activity
- Denaturation is irreversible - once enzymes are denatured they cannot regain their proper shape and activity will stop

**A **and **D **are incorrect because both graphs show enzyme activity as being extremely high at very low temperatures and very high temperatures, which is not possible - at low temperatures, the frequency of collisions is low (due to molecules having less kinetic energy) and at higher temperatures enzymes denature (due to destabilisation of enzyme structure permanently distorting the shape of the active site).

**C** is incorrect because this graph shows a gradual decrease in enzyme activity above the optimum temperature, which is incorrect as enzyme activity past the optimum decreases rapidly leading to denaturation.

parts.solutionMd:

parts.problemMd:
To investigate the effect of light and dark conditions on gas exchange in an aquatic plant, a test tube is set up as follows:

1. The test tube is filled with hydrogencarbonate indicator solution
2. A cutting from a green aquatic plant is added
3. The tube is covered with aluminium foil and closed with a bung
4. The tube is exposed to sunlight for 24 hours

What result will the test tube show after 24 hours?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B.**

- The aluminium foil prevents sunlight from entering the test tube
- The plant will respire but will be unable to photosynthesise
- More carbon dioxide is released than is used up
- This results in the hydrogencarbonate indicator solution changing colour to yellow

**A** is incorrect as no colour change will only occur in a control test tube without a plant cutting.

**C** is incorrect as the colour red in this instance indicates that photosynthesis and respiration are occurring at the same rate.

**D** is incorrect as the colour change to purple can only occur if the rate of photosynthesis is greater than that of respiration.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which of the following is a correct function of bile?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** (To increase the surface area of lipids for digestion) because:**

Bile works by **breaking** up **large** globules of lipids (fats and oils) into much **smaller** ones, **increasing** the **surface** **area** and making it easier for lipase enzymes to digest them into fatty acids. This is known as **emulsification**.

**A** is incorrect because bile emulsifies lipids, not proteins. Protein digestion begins in the stomach, where the conditions are acidic.

**B** is incorrect because even though bile does neutralise the food entering the duodenum, the food from the stomach is **acidic**, not alkaline. Bile is an alkaline solution.

**C** is incorrect because bile does not contain any enzymes.

**B** is incorrect because no absorption of water occurs in the pancreas. Remember the pancreas is an accessory organ, and not part of the alimentary canal so no food passes through it.

parts.problemMd: Which of the following is **not** an example of physical digestion?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** (Starch being broken down into glucose molecules.) because:**

The digestion of starch involves enzymes that break large insoluble starch molecules up into smaller soluble glucose molecules. Whenever enzymes are involved then it is an example of chemical digestion, not physical digestion.

**A**, **B** and **D** are incorrect because these are all examples of physical digestion where large food particles are mechanically broken down into smaller particles. This is done to increase the surface area on which the digestive enzymes can work during chemical digestion to change large insoluble molecules into smaller soluble ones.

parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** (W and Y) because:**

**Protein** digestion begins in the **stomach** (**W**) by action of acid and the enzyme pepsin. It also occurs in the small intestine (mainly in the **duodenum - Y**) as a result of proteases (such as trypsin) produced by the **pancreas** and the small intestine.

**B** and **C** are incorrect because **Z** is the **liver**, which produces **bile** to aid lipid digestion. The liver doesn’t play an active part in digestion.

parts.problemMd:
Which of the following is a correct cause and effect?

|   | **deficiency** | **cause** | **effect** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | iron | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver | brittle bones (rickets) |
| **B** | iron | lack of sunlight, fish and eggs | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues |
| **C** | vitamin D | lack of sunlight | brittle bones (rickets) |
| **D** | vitamin D | diet deficient in red meat, leafy green vegetables and liver | anaemia - tiredness and weakness due to not enough oxygen being delivered to tissues |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C ****because:**

A vitamin **D** **deficiency** leads to **brittle** **bones**, as it is required for bones to be able to **absorb** **calcium** ions in the **bloodstream**. Calcium is the mineral which is needed to strengthen bones; the less calcium the weaker they are. Vitamin D can be **synthesized** in the body when **cholesterol** in skin cells is **converted** into **Vitamin D**; this reaction is driven by **UV** from sunlight.

**A** is incorrect because the effect is not linked to a deficiency in iron.

**B** is incorrect because the cause is incorrect.

**D** is incorrect because the deficiency does not match the cause or the effect.

parts.problemMd:
Which of the following descriptions are correctly matched to the different stages of food breakdown?

|   | **absorption** | **assimilation** | **egestion** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| **B** | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| **C** | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | passing out of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
| **D** | small soluble food molecules cross the cell membrane of cells | small soluble food molecules move into the bloodstream | excretion of undigested or unabsorbed food through the anus |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** because:**

**Absorption** is the movement of soluble food molecules and ions through the intestinal wall into the blood to be transported to the cells. Once it reaches the cells these food molecules and ions will cross the cell membrane during **assimilation** in order to become part of the cell. Any food that hasn't been digested or absorbed will move along the alimentary canal and leave the body through the anus during **egestion**.

**A** is incorrect because egestion does not involve excretion. The waste products that leave the body during the process of excretion comes from metabolic reactions that occur **within cells**. Waste products that leave the body during egestion was created **outside cells**.

**C** is incorrect because the description of absorption and assimilation has been switched around.

**D** is incorrect because all three descriptions is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which of the following could be the correct effect and explanation of a disease that results in a reduced number of villi in the small intestine?

|   | **effect** | **explanation** |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | weight gain | reduced absorption of digested food molecules |
| **B** | weight gain | reduced digestion of maltose to glucose, less glucose absorbed |
| **C** | weight loss | reduced lipid digestion and absorption |
| **D** | weight loss | reduced absorption of digested food molecules |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** because:**

**Villi** **increase** the **surface** **area** over which **absorption** of digested food molecules into the **blood** can occur in the small intestine. A **reduction** in the number of villi would result in a **decreased** **surface** **area** for absorption so **less** **absorption** would occur as food passes through the lumen of the small intestine and more would be lost from the body. This could lead to weight loss.

**A** is incorrect because a person would not gain weight if they cannot absorb food molecules adequately. Weight gain is caused by an unbalanced diet; with the energy associated with food intake exceeded that expended.

**B** is incorrect because there may be reduced maltose digestion (as maltase is produced by cells lining the villi, reduced villi surface area would lead to less maltase) but this would not lead to weight gain.

**C** is incorrect because lipid digestion is unlikely to be affected, although lipid absorption would be.

**A** is incorrect because it represents a **capillary** entering the villus.

**B** is incorrect because it is a lacteal **entering** the villus to absorb the products of lipid digestion.

**D** is incorrect because it is a **capillary** leaving the villus. Although some fatty acid molecules will be absorbed into the bloodstream, far more end up in the lacteals.

parts.problemMd:
A student ate a meal which contained a type of biomolecule, **X**.

The digestion of biomolecule **X **started in the mouth, and finished in the duodenum.

What is the product of the digestion of biomolecule **X**?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** (Glucose) because:**

**Starch**, a large biomolecule, is made from many molecules of **glucose** molecules bonded together. **Salivary** **amylase**, an enzyme produced by the salivary glands, acts on starch and breaks it down into **maltose** (a disaccharide). **Amylase** is also produced by the **pancreas**, to help digest any remaining starch in the small intestine. Maltose is broken down by the enzyme **maltase** (which is found in the lining of the small intestine), producing **glucose** molecules.

**A** and **B** are incorrect because amino acids are the product of protein digestion, which begins in the stomach, not the mouth.

**D** is incorrect because starch was the starting molecule in this process (starch is a polymer of glucose molecules).

parts.problemMd:
Below is a list of chemical reactions that occur during digestion.

1. Protein → amino acids
2. Starch → maltose
3. Lipids → fatty acids + glycerol
4. Maltose → glucose

Which of the chemical reactions above might occur in the duodenum?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** (All 4) because:**

All the reactions listed can occur in the duodenum.

The **pancreas** produces **lipases**, pancreatic **amylase** and **proteases**; these enzymes mix with food that leaves the stomach in the duodenum, allowing digestion to continue to occur.

Starch digestion begins in the mouth, but not all starch there will be digested by salivary amylase (and this enzyme is denatured by acid in the stomach). Protein digestion begins in the stomach and continues in the duodenum.

**Maltase** is an enzyme produced by cells lining the small intestine, allowing **maltose** (a disaccharide) to be broken down into **glucose**.

parts.problemMd:
Which of the following shows the correct role of a substance made during digestion?

|   | **substance** | **made by** | **effect** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | trypsin | stomach | digests proteins into amino acids |
| **B** | bile | gallbladder | neutralising acidic mixture of food entering the duodenum from the stomach |
| **C** | gastric juice | stomach | denaturing enzymes in harmful microorganisms and optimising pH for pepsin activity |
| **D** | bile | liver | neutralising alkaline mixture of food entering the duodenum from the stomach |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C ****because:**

**Gastric** juice contains **hydrochloric** **acid**, which lowers the **pH** of the stomach to make conditions unsuitable for any microorganisms present in food, as well as **optimising** the pH for **pepsin**, a protease that works best around pH 2.

**A** is incorrect because **trypsin** is a protease that is made and secreted by the **pancreas** and it functions in the** small intestine**, not the stomach.

**B** is incorrect because **bile** is stored in the gallbladder, but it is made in the **liver**. The effect described is correct.

**D** is incorrect because bile neutralises acidic food and gastric juices entering the **duodenum** from the **stomach**.

parts.solutionMd:

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which of the following is a correct explanation of the process of translocation in a plant?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** because:**

- Sugars are synthesised in the leaf via photosynthesis and then converted into substances such as **sucrose **and **amino acids** (using nitrate ions). The leaf is therefore a **source **- a region of production
- Sucrose and amino acids are then transported to other regions of the plant through the phloem (through which movement can occur in **both **directions)
- Sucrose and amino acids are transported to regions of **storage**, or to regions where they can be used in **respiration **(sugars) or for **growth **(amino acids) - a **sink**

**A** is incorrect because translocation involves the movement of sugars and amino acids through the phloem.

**C** is incorrect because movement through the phloem is two-way (unlike movement in the xylem, which is one-way)

**D** is incorrect because movement through the phloem occurs from a source to a sink. Some parts of a plant may act as a source or a sink at different times during the lifecycle of a plant.

A potometer can be used to measure the rate that a piece of plant transpires under various conditions.

Part of a potometer is shown in the diagram below.

![potometer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/8-transport-in-plants/8-1-transport-in-plants/assets/029-potometer.png)

parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct (false) statement is ****B.**** (in a potometer, an air bubble moves away from the piece of plant tissue that is under investigation) because:**

The air bubble moves **towards** the plant. the transpiration stream pulls water into the xylem at the bottom of the piece of plant. The bubble moves with the water, therefore towards the plant.

**A**, **C** and **D** are all correct statements.

For **A**, the transpiration of water pulls water up from the potometer, provided there is a tight seal between the end of the cut stem of the plant and the water supply beneath.

For **C**, the rate of reaction (or any process) always requires a measurement of time so that, in this case, the speed of uptake of water per minute/hour can be measured and stated quantitatively.

For **D**, water on the leaves may block stomata and prevent water vapour from diffusing out, hence affecting the rate of transpiration.

parts.problemMd: Which sequence correctly shows the pathway of water through a plant?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B.**

- Water moves through the plant in this order:

**root hair cells → root cortex cells → xylem → mesophyll cells**

- **Root hair cells** absorb water from the soil because they are in direct contact and have a large surface area.
- The water then passes through the **root cortex cells** to reach the centre of the root
- Next, the water enters the **xylem**, which carries water up through the root and stem towards the leaves
- Finally, in the leaf water moves from the xylem into the **mesophyll cells**, where it can evaporate during transpiration and is also used in photosynthesis

Which of the following processes is/are involved in the loss of water from the leaves of plants?

1. diffusion
2. osmosis
3. condensation
4. evaporation
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** (1 and 4) because:**

Water molecules evaporate from mesophyll cells, forming water vapour (a gas) which diffuses from an area of higher concentration in the air spaces inside the leaf to a lower concentration in the air outside the leaf (unless it’s very humid and the air is saturated with water!)

**A** is incorrect because diffusion is involved in the loss of water from a leaf, but condensation (change in the stage of gas to a liquid) is not.

parts.problemMd: A **decrease **in which of the following factors would normally cause the transpiration rate to **increase**?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D ****because:**

The less humid (drier) the atmosphere, the higher the diffusion gradient between the inside of the leaf and the outside (through the stomatal pore).

**A** is incorrect because a decrease in stomatal density means less transpiration (as the leaves have fewer stomata).

**B** is incorrect because a reduction in light intensity causes stomata to close, reducing the rate of transpiration.

**C** is incorrect because a reduction in temperature means the water vapour molecules move more slowly, so they would diffuse out of the stomata at a lower rate.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which environmental factor is most likely to be responsible for a plant to wilt?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** because:**

If a plant does not get enough water, it becomes limp and wilts. This is because water has left the cells and they have become flaccid, providing less support to the overall structure of the leaf. If a cell does not contain enough water there is no pressure pushing outwards against the cell wall and the cells will all shrink a little.

**A** is incorrect because a decrease in light intensity would just reduce the rate of photosynthesis, not cause the plant to wilt.

**B** is incorrect because an increase in humidity would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water.

**D** is incorrect because a decrease in wind speed would reduce transpiration from the plant, meaning it would retain more water.

parts.problemMd:
A plant shoot is placed in a solution of dye.

The dye moves up the stem.

Under which conditions will the dye move most slowly?

|   | temperature | humidity |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | high | high |
| **B** | high | low |
| **C** | low | high |
| **D** | low | low |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C****.**

- The dye will move more slowly when transpiration is slowest
- More humid conditions will reduce transpiration due to a decrease in the concentration gradient between the air outside the leaf and the air spaces in the spongy mesophyll
- A low temperature will reduce transpiration as it decreases the rate of evaporation from the surface of the cells in the spongy mesophyll

**A **is incorrect because high temperature would increase the rate of transpiration whilst high humidity would reduce rates of transpiration and fluid movement in the plant.

**B** is incorrect because high temperature and low humidity would likely facilitate faster movement of the dye due to increased evaporation and transpiration rates.

**D** is incorrect because even though low humidity would increase transpiration, low temperature reduces the kinetic energy of molecules, leading to slower movement.

parts.problemMd:
Which environmental condition would most reduce transpiration?

|   | temperature | humidity |
|---|---|---|
| A | low | high |
| B | high | low |
| C | low | low |
| D | high | high |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A.**

- Transpiration is reduced by **low temperature** and **high humidity**
- **Low temperature** gives water molecules less kinetic energy, so evaporation from mesophyll cell surfaces is slower
- **High humidity** means the air already contains a lot of water vapour, so the diffusion gradient for water vapour leaving the leaf is smaller, reducing diffusion through the stomata

**B **is incorrect because high temperature and low humidity both increase transpiration.

**C** is incorrect because low humidity increases the diffusion gradient for water vapour.

**D** is incorrect because high temperature increases evaporation.

parts.problemMd:
A potometer is used to measure the rate of transpiration. The table below shows the results.

| **Distance travelled by bubble (mm)** | **Time (mins)** |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 17 | 30 |
| 29 | 60 |
| 35 | 90 |
| 44 | 120 |
| 51 | 150 |

Calculate the rate of transpiration between 30 and 120 minutes.
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C.**

- To calculate the rate of transpiration:

$\text{rate of transpiration} = \frac{\text{distance travelled by bubble}}{\text{time}}$

- Calculate the distance travelled by the bubble between 120 min and 30 min:

= 44 - 17

= 27 mm

- Calculate the time that passes between 120 and 30 mins:

= 120 - 30

= 90 min

- Calculate the rate of transpiration:

= 27 ÷ 90

=** 0.3 ****mm / min**

**A** is incorrect as it corresponds to dividing 44 mm by 120 mins, i.e. it is the rate of transpiration between 0 and 120 mins, not between 30 and 120 mins.

**C** is incorrect as this is what you get if you divide time by distance (90 ÷ 27) rather than distance by time.

**D** is incorrect as this is the correct calculation but the wrong unit.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always remember to calculate the change in distance and the change in time rather than using the raw values from the table.
> 
> Ensure that you include the correct units in your final answer.

| **D** | 2 | 4 | 1 |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A ****because:**

- Cell 1 is a **red blood cell** (not named in the table)
- Cell 2 is a **phagocyte**. Phagocytes have a lobed nucleus, their job is to engulf and destroy foreign material (including pathogens)
- 3 are the **platelets**, fragments of cells that help form clots when blood vessels are damaged
- Cell 4 is a **lymphocyte**. Lymphocytes have a very large nucleus (this is because they produce antibodies which requires a number of genes to be involved in large-scale protein synthesis)

parts.problemMd:
What happens to the heart valves when the ventricles contract?

|   | atrioventricular valves | semilunar valves |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | close | close |
| **B** | close | open |
| **C** | open | close |
| **D** | open | open |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- This is because when the ventricles contract the AV valves close to prevent blood flowing backwards into the atria
- When the ventricles contract the SL valves open to allow the blood to flow out of the heart via the aorta and pulmonary arteries

**A** is incorrect because SL valves must be open to allow the blood to leave the heart

**C **is incorrect because the AV valves must be closed otherwise blood would flow backwards and SL valves must be open to allow the blood to leave the heart

**D **is incorrect because the AV valves must be closed otherwise blood would flow backwards

parts.problemMd:

| **B** | pulmonary vein | pulmonary artery |
| **C** | renal artery | renal vein |
| **D** | renal vein | renal artery |
parts.solutionMd:

- The renal artery carries blood to the kidney and the renal vein carries blood away from the kidney

**A** and **B** are incorrect because the pulmonary artery takes blood from the heart to the lungs and the pulmonary vein takes blood from the heart to the lungs.

**D** is incorrect because the renal vein carries blood to the kidney and the renal artery carries blood from the kidney.

parts.problemMd: Which process is slower than normal in a person with very few platelets?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B****.**

- This is because the role of platelets in the blood is to aid with blood clotting and so if someone had fewer platelets it would result in them having slower blood clotting than usual

**A** is incorrect because platelets are not related to the function of antibodies in the blood, this is the role of white blood cells.

**C** is incorrect because platelets are not related to the function of oxygen transport in the blood, this is the role of red blood cells.

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows the circulatory system of a fish.

Where in the circulatory system is the oxygen concentration lowest?

- When the blood is in vessel X it has passed through the body of the fish since it was last in the gills and full of oxygen

- In the diagram, **X leads out of the organ**, which matches the position of the hepatic vein

**B** is incorrect because the hepatic portal vein also enters the liver at the bottom. It brings nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver and is typically shown entering the liver alongside the hepatic artery.

parts.problemMd:
The following are statements about blood.

1. Red blood cells transport oxygen.
2. Plasma transports hormones.
3. Platelets destroy pathogens.

Which statements are correct?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B.**

**Statement 1 is correct **because **red blood cells transport oxygen**. They contain **haemoglobin**, a protein that** binds oxygen** in the lungs and carries it to body tissues.

**Statement 2 is correct **because **plasma transports hormones and other dissolved substances** around the body. These include nutrients such as glucose, waste products such as urea, carbon dioxide and ions.

**Statement 3 is incorrect **because **destroying pathogens is mainly the role of white blood cells**. **Platelets **are involved in **blood clotting**, helping to form a clot to prevent blood loss when a blood vessel is damaged.

parts.problemMd: Which of the following would be found dissolved in the blood plasma of a human?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A.**** (Glucose, urea and hormones) because:**

- Plasma is mainly water with many substances dissolved in it
- Soluble nutrients such as glucose, amino acids and mineral ions, hormones, carbon dioxide, urea are all carried in plasma

**B** is incorrect because oxygen is transported by haemoglobin in red blood cells. Starch is a large, insoluble molecule that cannot be transported in the plasma (it does not dissolve in the water of blood plasma).

**C** is incorrect because haemoglobin is the pigment found in red blood cells that binds reversibly to oxygen. Carbon dioxide is transported around the body dissolved in blood plasma.

**D** is incorrect because oxygen is mainly carried by haemoglobin in the red blood cells. Carbon dioxide is transported around the body and dissolved in blood plasma.

parts.problemMd: Which blood vessel has a relatively low carbon dioxide concentration, a high oxygen concentration and a low blood pressure?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B. ****(pulmonary vein) because:**

- The blood pressure in **veins** is always **lower** than the blood pressure in **arteries** (as blood is being transported back to the heart in the veins, and is no longer under the direct influence of the heart beat)
- The **pulmonary** **vein** is the only vein in the body that transports **oxygenated** blood, as it’s transporting blood that has picked up oxygen and lost carbon dioxide from the **lungs** back to the **heart**. This is a feature of the double circulatory system in mammals to ensure the respiring tissues of the body receive an efficient supply of oxygen

**A** is incorrect because the pulmonary artery transports deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs for gas exchange.

**C** is incorrect because the aorta transports oxygenated blood from the heart towards arteries that supply the tissues at high pressure.

**D** is incorrect because the vena cava is the vein that returns deoxygenated blood from the body’s tissues to the heart.

parts.problemMd: In which list of the following do all three blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood?
parts.solutionMd:

- The vena cava is the vein that returns deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium of the heart
- The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. It is the only artery of the body that carries deoxygenated blood
- The renal vein carries deoxygenated blood from the kidneys back towards the heart (the renal vein joins the vein cava)

**A** is incorrect because the aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body, the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the heart and the renal artery carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.

**B** is incorrect because the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left side of the heart (the only vein in the body which carries oxygenated blood).

**D** is incorrect because the aorta and renal artery carry oxygenated blood.

parts.problemMd:
Below are statements about the components of blood and their functions.

1. White blood cells produce antibodies and carry out phagocytosis
2. Red blood cells transport oxygen using haemoglobin
3. Platelets transport hormones and nutrients around the body
4. Plasma transports carbon dioxide and urea

Which statements are correct?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C.**

- **Statement 1** is correct: white blood cells defend the body against pathogens by producing antibodies and carrying out phagocytosis to engulf pathogens
- **Statement 2 **is correct: red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds to oxygen and transports it around the body
- **Statement 4** is correct: plasma is the liquid component of blood that transports substances including carbon dioxide and urea

**Statement 3** is incorrect as it is plasma, not platelets, that transports hormones and nutrients around the body. Platelets are involved in clotting to prevent blood loss and the entry of pathogens.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

The immune system recognises which part of a pathogen?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B.**** (Antigen) because:**

**Antigens** are **chemicals** on the surface of all cells. The antigens of cells that don’t belong to the body are recognised as **foreign**, and can stimulate an immune response.

**A** is incorrect because antibiotics are chemicals produced by bacterial cells or fungi to kill other bacteria or prevent them from replicating.

**C** is incorrect because the active site is part of an enzyme to which a complementary substrate can temporarily bind to.

**D** is incorrect because antibodies are chemicals made by lymphocytes to attach to antigens on foreign cells, restricting their movement and signalling them for destruction.

parts.problemMd: What is a pathogen?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C.**** (A disease-causing organism) because:**

A pathogen is a microorganism that infects another organism where it replicates / multiplies and causes disease.

**A** is incorrect because a transmissible disease is caused by a pathogen that can spread from one organism to another (e.g. Covid-19 is a transmissible disease caused by the pathogenic SARS-CoV-2 virus).

**B** is incorrect because phagocytes are part of the immune system responsible for destroying pathogens that have entered the body.

**D** is incorrect because not all bacteria (or microorganisms for that matter) are pathogenic. The human digestive system and skin, contains huge numbers of beneficial bacteria that help prevent infection (by competing with pathogens for resources).

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

In many multicellular animals, pathogens are recognised as foreign and are attacked by the immune system.

Which of the following may be produced during an immune response?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D.**** (Antibodies) because:**

Lymphocytes will produce antibodies in response to the presence of a foreign antigen in the body.

**A** is incorrect because antigens are chemicals on the surface of all cells that helps the immune system determine if a cell is 'self' or 'non-self' and therefore foreign.

**B** is incorrect because antibiotics are chemical substances made by certain fungi or bacterial cells that affect the working of other bacterial cells either by disrupting their structure or preventing them from reproducing.

**C** is incorrect because pathogens are disease causing organisms, they are not produced during an immune response.

parts.problemMd: Which body defence listed below acts as a chemical barrier?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A.**** (Mucus lining the airways) because:**

Barriers are methods by which the body prevents the entry of microorganisms. A chemical barrier is, as the name suggests, a chemical produced by the body as opposed to a physical structure. Examples of chemical barriers include mucus produced by cells in the airways or the enzymes in tears.

**B** is incorrect because although antibodies are chemicals produced by the body, they do not count as a barrier as they do not act to prevent the entry of microorganisms, but are produced by lymphocytes once they have already entered the body.

**C** is incorrect because hairs in the nose are classed as physical barriers.

**D** is incorrect because phagocytosis is a process which involves surrounding, engulfing and digesting of bacteria.

parts.problemMd: Which of the options below is an example of a transmissible disease?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C.**** (Cholera) because:**

A transmissible disease is a disease caused by a pathogen that can be passed from person to person. Cholera is a disease caused by the pathogen *Vibrio cholerae*, a bacterium which can be transmitted via water contaminated with faeces.

**A** is incorrect because obesity is largely a lifestyle disease caused by a poor diet (excess food consumption) and lack of exercise. Genetics may play a role in some cases.

**B** is incorrect because tooth decay is caused by poor dental hygiene.

**D** is incorrect because rickets is a deficiency disease caused by a lack of Vitamin D in the diet, leading to poor absorption of calcium into the bones, leaving them brittle and weak.

parts.problemMd:
The body has several defence mechanisms to protect against disease.

Which defence mechanism is a chemical barrier?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B****.**

- This is because mucus is a chemical produced to trap pathogens so they can be destroyed before they are able enter the bloodstream and cause an infection

**A **and** C **are** **incorrect because these are both physical barriers to prevent pathogens from entering the body.

**D** is incorrect because white blood cells are not a barrier to prevent pathogens from entering the body. They provide an immune response after the pathogen has already successfully entered past the barriers.

**B** is incorrect because antigens are present in the blood from the moment of the vaccination because the vaccine contains antigens for the pathogen being immunised against.

**C** is incorrect because there are no live pathogens used in vaccines and so there should not be any present in the blood during this process. Some vaccines do contain dead pathogens or fragments of pathogens.

**D** is incorrect because platelets are not involved in the immune response, they aid with blood clotting.

parts.problemMd: Which cells produce mucus?
parts.solutionMd:

- This is because goblet cells produce mucus, for example in the trachea where the mucus is used to trap dust and pathogens and prevent them from entering the lungs

**A** is incorrect because ciliated cells move mucus but do not produce it themselves.

**D** is incorrect because white blood cells help to kill pathogens but do not produce mucus.

parts.problemMd:
The human body has a number of barriers to prevent infection by pathogens some of which are listed below.

Which of these are examples of mechanical barriers?

**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A.**** (1 and 3) because:**

The skin and hairs in the nose forms a physical barrier that makes it more difficult for pathogens to enter the body.

**B** and **C** are incorrect because mucus (2) is an example of a chemical barrier while antibodies (4) are produced by lymphocytes in response to foreign antigens entering the body, they do not act as a barrier.

parts.problemMd:

parts.problemMd: Which of the following diseases can be transmitted by contact with contaminated surfaces?

Both these diseases are transmitted when a person comes into contact with a surface that contains these pathogens.

**A** is incorrect because malaria is transmitted by the bite of the female *Anopheles* mosquito.

parts.problemMd:
Statements 1 to 4 describe stages in the development of cholera.

parts.problemMd:

parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A.**** (1 and 2 only) because:**

- You can develop **active** **immunity** by being **vaccinated** (1) with a weakened pathogen/antigens from the pathogen, or by being **infected** by a pathogen (2) that causes disease in you which you then get over

The oesophagus is part of the digestive system, not the breathing system.

parts.problemMd:
Which of the following helps carbon dioxide to be excreted rapidly into the alveoli from the blood in the lungs?

1. Inhaled air has a lower concentration of carbon dioxide than the blood constantly pumping through the lungs.
2. Alveoli have thick walls and a large surface area.
3. Alveoli have thin walls and a large surface area.
4. The concentration of carbon dioxide in the blood is lower than in the alveoli.
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C.**** (1 & 3 only) because:**

- Inhaled air has a lower concentration of carbon dioxide than that in the blood passing through the capillaries in the lungs, creating a diffusion gradient that enables diffusion to happen as quickly as possible
- Thin walls mean that diffusion happens quickly as diffusion distances are short, and a large surface area means more carbon dioxide can diffuse out of the blood into the alveolar surface in the time available

parts.problemMd:
Below are statements about the features of gas exchange surfaces in humans.

1. Gas exchange surfaces have a large surface area to maximise the rate of diffusion
2. Gas exchange surfaces have a thick surface to prevent damage from the constant movement of air
3. Gas exchange surfaces have a good blood supply to remove gases that have diffused across the surface
4. Gas exchange surfaces are well ventilated to increase the concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli

Which statements are correct?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C.**

- **Statement 1** is correct: a large surface area increases the rate of diffusion of gases across the gas exchange surface
- **Statement 3** is correct: a good blood supply removes oxygen from the lung capillaries after it has diffused into the blood, maintaining the concentration gradient for further diffusion

**Statement 2** is incorrect as gas exchange surfaces are thin, not thick in order to maximise the rate of diffusion.

**Statement 4** is incorrect as good ventilation maintains a high concentration of oxygen and a low concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli, not a high concentration of carbon dioxide.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which of the following statements is a correct reason that humans sweat?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C ****because:**

Sweating is an important process that helps cool the body by increasing heat loss to the environment. When a person’s core body temperature increases above the normal range, sweat glands in the skin release sweat (a solution of water and salts). Water molecules in sweat can evaporate (change state from a liquid to a gas); this results in a cooling effect as heat energy is lost from the body in this process.

**A **is incorrect because this statement implies that the purpose of water loss through the skin is to lose water! The release of sweat containing water is to cool the body.

**B** is incorrect because the loss of water from the kidneys is not a reason why people sweat. Indeed when a person sweats their kidneys may need to respond by losing less water to maintain blood pressure and prevent dehydration.

**D** is incorrect because sweating does not reduce blood glucose levels!

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which of the following statements would **not **be a correct example of negative feedback?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** because:**

The release of a neurotransmitter at a synapse is not an example of negative feedback. Negative feedback mechanisms are the responses that occur in the body when a factor/system moves away from the normal range in which it should fall.

**A** is incorrect because maintenance of a core body temperature within a narrow range is a key example of negative feedback.

**B** is incorrect because vasoconstriction (constriction of arterioles in the skin) is part of a negative feedback response to a decrease in body temperature and is an action to reduce heat loss.

**D** is incorrect because the hormones insulin and glucagon act to maintain blood glucose levels within a narrow range, another key example of negative feedback.

parts.problemMd:
Which row of the table best summarises the parts of the nervous system?

|   | **brain** | **neurones** | **spinal cord** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | central | peripheral | central |
| **B** | peripheral | peripheral | central |
| **C** | central | central | central |
| **D** | peripheral | central | peripheral |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A ****because:**

- The brain and spinal cord together comprise the **central nervous system** (CNS)
- The network of neurones that extends to all parts of the body makes up the **peripheral nervous system**

parts.problemMd:
Which of the following statements are reasons for the evolution of reflex arcs in the mammalian nervous system?

1. To prevent harm or damage to an organism.
2. To provide a rapid response to dangerous situations.
3. To allow a degree of choice to an organism about response.
4. To allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated.
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** (1 and 2 are correct) because:**

- **Statement 1** (to prevent harm or damage to an organism) is correct because an automatic, rapid response to a dangerous stimulus cuts the reaction time and allows less damage to be sustained before a response takes place
- **Statement 2** (to provide a rapid response to dangerous situations) is correct, linked to the explanation for **Statement 1**

**Statement 3** (to allow a degree of choice to an organism about response) is incorrect because reflexes are involuntary - they take place with no choice of conscious thought.

**Statement 4** (to allow certain stimuli to be ignored/eliminated) is incorrect because a dangerous stimulus cannot be ignored, nor can one be eliminated; that would be outside an organism's ability to control events!

- The nose detects gaseous (vapour) molecules that diffuse into the nostrils and fall on sensory receptors in the nasal passages

parts.problemMd: What is the sequence of neurones connecting a receptor to an effector in a reflex arc?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D****.**

- The pathway in a reflex arc goes from a sensory neuron (which detects the stimulus), to a relay neuron (which processes the signal in the spinal cord), and then to a motor neuron (which activates the effector).

All other options are incorrect because they do not give the correct sequence of neurones.

parts.problemMd:
What controls how much light enters the eye?

![Cross-sectional diagram of an eye showing labelled parts: A is the cornea, B is the iris, C is the lens, and D is the optic nerve, with surrounding tissues.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/14-coordination-and-response/14-1-coordination-response-and-homeostasis/assets/008-cross-sectional-diagram-of-an-eye-showing-labell.png)
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B****.**

- B is the iris which contains muscles that can contract and relax to control how much light enters the eye through the pupil.
- Extended students also need to be able to explain how the antagonistic action of radial and circular muscles in the iris control the pupil reflex.

**A** is the cornea which refracts light as it enters the eye.

**C** is the lens which focuses light onto the retina.

**D** is the optic nerve that carries impulses to the brain.

parts.problemMd: Which hormone triggers the ‘fight or flight’ response?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C****.**

- This is because adrenaline triggers the fight or flight response.

**A** is incorrect because testosterone controls secondary sexual characteristics in males.

**B** is incorrect because oestrogen controls secondary sexual characteristics in women.

**D** is incorrect because insulin helps to lower blood glucose.

parts.problemMd: Which organ detects and coordinates the response to changes in internal body temperature?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A****.**

- This is because the brain acts as a coordinator in the nervous system that detects and coordinates the response to changes in internal body temperature

**B** is incorrect because the role of the heart is to pump blood around the body, not to detect and coordinate changes in internal body temperature.

**C** is incorrect because the role of the liver is to produce bile and help with the breakdown and processing of waste products in the body, not to detect and coordinate changes in internal body temperature.

**D** is incorrect because the role of the skin is to act as a barrier to protect the body, not to detect and coordinate changes in internal body temperature.

parts.problemMd:
What is the effect of adrenaline on pulse rate and blood glucose concentration?

|   | pulse rate | blood glucose |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | decreases | decreases |
| **B** | decreases | increases |
| **C** | increases | decreases |
| **D** | increases | increases |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D****.**

- Adrenaline increases pulse rate in order to move more blood to the respiring muscle tissues and increases blood glucose concentration to drive respiration in preparation for 'fight or flight' responses.

**A** is incorrect because adrenaline increases both pulse rate and blood glucose concentration, not decreases them. Decreasing both would reduce the rate of respiration in vital muscle tissues and not allow the body to prepare for fight or flight.

**B** is incorrect because decreasing the pulse rate would reduce the speed at which blood is delivered to the respiring muscle tissues. This would decrease the oxygen and glucose supply and prevent the body from preparing for fight or flight.

**C** is incorrect because although adrenaline increases pulse rate, it also increases blood glucose concentration. If blood glucose were to decrease, this would lead to a reduced respiration rate and prevent the body from preparing for fight or flight.

parts.problemMd:
The image below shows a simple reflex arc.

![14--image-1---reflex-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/14-coordination-and-response/14-1-coordination-response-and-homeostasis/assets/014-14-image-1-reflex-1.png)

Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order of cells that an impulse passes through during a reflex action?

|   | **first  →  last** |
|---|---|
| **A** | Z   →    X   →    Y |
| **B** | X   →   Y    →   Z |
| **C** | Y  →     X   →    Z |
| **D** | Z   →    Y   →    X |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

- Receptor cells are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that is then sent along a sensory neurone (Z) to the coordinator (the brain or spinal cord)
- The impulse is then passed to a relay neurone (X) which is a short neurone found inside the coordinator and connects sensory neurones to motor neurones
- The impulse is then passed on to a motor neurone (Y) which connects to an effector, in this case a muscle, stimulating it to contract and bring about a response

**B** is incorrect because a reflex action cannot start with the relay neurone (X).

**C** is incorrect because the order of neurones is back-to-front from effector (muscle) to receptor, only effectors can carry out a response when signalled by an impulse from a motor neurone (Y) which requires impulses originating from the receptor.

**D** is incorrect because impulses pass along neurones in sequential order, an impulse cannot jump from a sensory neurone to a motor neurone.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

The image below shows some of the structures in the eye.

![14--image-2---the-eye](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/14-coordination-and-response/14-1-coordination-response-and-homeostasis/assets/016-14-image-2-the-eye.png)

The circular and radial muscles can control the size of the pupil in the eye.

How would they respond in the eye of a person walking from a brightly lit room into a dark one?

|   | **radial muscles** | **circular muscles** | **pupil ** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | relaxes | contracts | constricts |
| **B** | relaxes | contracts | dilated |
| **C** | contracts | relaxes | dilated |
| **D** | contracts | relaxes | constricts |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C**** because:**

- In dim light the pupil needs to dilate to allow more light to reach the retina. To achieve this, the radial muscles must contract and the circular muscles must relax (as they work <u>antagonistically</u>)
- In bright light the circular muscles contract, constricting (the 3 C’s!) the pupil to reduce the amount of light entering the eye so that the photoreceptor cells of the retina are not damaged

**A** is incorrect because this would be the correct response of the muscles in the eyes if the person were in bright light.

**B** is incorrect because when circular muscles contract and the radial muscles relax, the iris becomes thicker so that the pupil constricts.

**D** is incorrect because when the radial muscles contract the iris is pulled thin to allow the pupil to dilate so that more light can enter the eye.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which row of the following table correctly describes what happens in the body after a person consumes a can of sugary drink?

|   | **role of the pancreas** | **role of the liver** | **effect** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | releases glucagon | converts glycogen into glucose | blood sugar levels rise |
| **B** | releases insulin | converts excess glucose into glycogen | blood sugar level falls |
| **C** | releases glucagon | converts excess glucose into glycogen | blood sugar level falls |
| **D** | releases insulin | converts glycogen into glucose | blood sugar levels rise |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** because:**

- Both hormones which control blood glucose concentration are made by cells in the pancreas. Insulin is secreted in response to blood glucose levels rising; insulin stimulates the liver (and muscle cells) to take up excess glucose and convert it into the polymer glycogen so that it can be stored
- Too much glucose in cells lowers the water potential, which if left unchecked could lead to too much water being drawn into the cell by osmosis which could result in the cell bursting. The control of blood glucose levels is an example of *negative feedback*
- Glucagon is produced by different cells in the pancreas when blood glucose levels fall below the ideal range, this hormone stimulates liver and muscle cells to convert stored glycogen back into glucose which can then be released into the blood

**A** is incorrect because this would be the effect in the body when the blood sugar level decreases below the healthy range.

**C** and **D** are incorrect because the hormones are the wrong way around.

parts.problemMd:
The image below shows a cell from the nervous system. The cell forms part of a reflex arc.

![14--image-3--neurone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/14-coordination-and-response/14-1-coordination-response-and-homeostasis/assets/015-14-image-3-neurone.png)

An impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P.

What structures would be found at P and Q?

|   | **P** | **Q** |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | receptor | relay neurone |
| **B** | relay neurone | receptor |
| **C** | motor neurone | relay neurone |
| **D** | gland | relay neurone |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****B**** because:**

The cell in the image above is a sensory neurone. If the impulse moves along the neurone from Q to P, then Q must be a receptor cell in a sense organ and P must be a relay neurone in the central nervous system (CNS).

**A** is incorrect because this answer would only be correct if the impulse travelled along the neurone from left to right (the question specifies it travels in the opposite direction).

**C** is incorrect because the relay neurone synapses with the motor neurone directly in a reflex arc; there is no neurone in between them.

**D** is incorrect because this would be correct if the cell shown was a motor neurone. Notice that the cell body is found strongly at one end of the motor neurone.

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

An athlete takes part in a marathon.

What would be the effect of an athlete taking part in a marathon race on a hot, sunny day?

|   | **volume of water reabsorbed in the kidneys** | **volume of water lost from the skin** | **effect on hairs on the skin** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | less | decreases | lie flat |
| **B** | more | decreases | erect |
| **C** | less | increases | lie flat |
| **D** | more | increases | lie flat |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** because:**

- During strenuous exercise the body temperature will rise (due to increased muscle activity) and therefore sweat will be produced to help cool the body down as evaporation of water from the skin results in increased heat loss leading to a cooling effect
- This increases the volume of water lost through the skin. To prevent dehydration and maintain blood pressure, less water will need to be lost from the kidneys in the production of urine. As such, more water would be reabsorbed back into the bloodstream from the kidney tubules (resulting in a smaller volume of more concentrated urine being produced)
- As body temperature rises, the skin responds by relaxing effector muscles so that the hairs on the skin lie flat. Less air is trapped against the skin, reducing the insulting effect so that more heat loss can occur

parts.problemMd:
#### Extended only

Which row of the following table correctly describes the effect of adrenaline in the body?

|   | **pulse rate** | **blood glucose concentration ** | **breathing rate** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | increases | remains constant | increases |
| **B** | increases | decreases | decreases |
| **C** | increases | increases | increases |
| **D** | decreases | increases | increases |
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****C ****because:**

- Adrenaline is known as the 'fight or flight' hormone because it is produced in situations where the organism may be in danger. It causes a range of different things to happen in the body, all designed to prepare it for movement (i.e. fight or flight)

Some of the effects of adrenaline include:

- Increasing blood glucose concentration for increased respiration in muscle cells
- Increasing pulse rate and breathing rate so glucose and oxygen can be delivered to muscle cells and carbon dioxide taken away from muscle cells more quickly
- Both of these effects maximise the ability of the muscles to contract to bring about rapid movement

Other effects of adrenaline include:

- Diverting blood flow towards muscles and away from non-essential parts of the body such as the alimentary canal
- Dilating pupils to allow as much light as possible to reach the retina so more information can be sent to the brain

![14--image-4--reflex-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/3b2ce8da700b80f51700fb34fc721c90d6654d6b/SME-ExamQuestion/cie-igcse-biology-23/14-coordination-and-response/14-1-coordination-response-and-homeostasis/assets/017-14-image-4-reflex-2.png)

Which of the following sequences correctly shows the order that an impulse passes through during a reflex action?
parts.solutionMd:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****A**** because:**

Receptor cells (S) are found in sense organs. They pick up on the stimulus which generates an electrical impulse that travels along a sensory neurone (U) to the central nervous system (the brain or spinal cord) where it synapses with a relay neurone (V) which allows the impulse to pass rapidly from the sensory neurone to a motor neurone. Motor neurones synapse with effectors, in this case a muscle (T), stimulating it to contract and bring about a response.

**B** is incorrect because T is the effector (muscle) and U is the sensory neurone; the sensory neurone does not connect to the effector via a synapse.

**C** is incorrect because the receptor cells (S) are connected to sensory neurones (U) only.

**D** is incorrect because a reflex arc cannot begin with an effector!
